title: On the Reliability of CyberGym Evaluation: Task Material Consistency and Reference-Target Identity
abstract: arXiv:2611.25790v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: CyberGym evaluates vulnerability reproduction by checking whether a proof-of-concept input (PoC) crashes a vulnerable program version but not a fixed version. Interpreting this differential pass as successful reproduction requires consistent task materials and evidence that the PoC triggers the intended defect. We examine these requirements through a material audit of all 1,507 CyberGym tasks and an identity assessment of the final PoCs from one complete Level-1 GLM-5.3 run. Taking the defect associated with each reference crash report as the target, the audit assigns inconsistency labels to 338 tasks (22.4%) after correcting two labels identified by stratified blind review. The largest categories are coverage inconsistency (205 tasks) and descriptions and patches that jointly point to another defect (110 tasks). We assess PoC identity using an execution check, crash-signature matching, and LLM-assisted root-cause review. Of the 1,286

translated_title: 论CyberGym评估的可靠性：任务材料一致性与参照目标同一性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.25790v1 公告类型：交叉  摘要：CyberGym通过检验概念验证输入是否能使存在漏洞的程序版本崩溃、而不使修复后的版本崩溃，来评估漏洞复现能力。将这种差异性通过解读为成功的漏洞复现，需要任务材料保持一致，并需要证据表明该PoC确实触发了预期的缺陷。我们通过对全部1,507个CyberGym任务进行材料审计，以及对一次完整的Level-1 GLM-5.3运行所生成的最终PoC进行同一性评估，来检验上述要求。以每份参考崩溃报告所关联的缺陷为目标，在对分层盲审中识别出的两个标签进行修正后，审计为338个任务（占22.4%）标注了不一致性标签。其中最大的类别是覆盖率不一致（205个任务），以及描述与补丁共同指向另一个缺陷（110个任务）。我们采用执行检查、崩溃签名匹配以及大语言模型辅助的根因审查来评估PoC的同一性。在1,286个……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究对CyberGym漏洞复现基准的全部1,507个任务进行了材料审计与PoC同一性评估，发现22.4%的任务存在材料不一致问题，揭示了该基准评估结果可靠性方面的缺陷。
en_tdlr: This paper conducts a material audit of all 1,507 CyberGym tasks and an identity assessment of final PoCs, finding that 22.4% of tasks suffer from material inconsistencies, thereby exposing reliability flaws in the benchmark's vulnerability reproduction evaluation.
